title: Calculate inverse sums

hook.scenario: Aap pizza ke alag-alag fractions add kar rahe ho, jaise `1/3` aur `1/6`.
hook.question: Lekin jab denominator alag ho, toh fractions add kaise karte hain?

mental_model.intuition: Fractions add karne ke liye sabka base ek jaisa banana padta hai.
mental_model.description: Inverse sums mein (jaise `1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2`), hum fractions ko directly nahi jod sakte. Pehle LCM (Least Common Multiple) le kar common denominator banate hain, fractions add karte hain, aur aakhir mein result ka ulta (reciprocal) karte hain.

explanation:
Physics mein parallel circuits solve karte waqt, `1/R = 1/R1 + 1/R2` jaisi equations banti hain. Isko solve karne ke liye fraction addition ke mathematical rules zaroori hain.

Sabse pehle, denominators `R1` aur `R2` ka LCM nikalte hain. LCM woh sabse chhota number hai jo dono denominators ki table mein aata hai. Jab common base mil jaye, tab hum numerators ko us hisaab se adjust karte hain aur add kar dete hain.

Ye step poora hone par humein `1/R` ki value milti hai. Lekin humein total resistance `R` chahiye hota hai. Isliye final fraction ko ulta (reciprocal) karna sabse critical step hai.

Bina reciprocal kiye answer chhod dena sabse common galti hoti hai. Hamesha dhyan rakho, formula `1/R` deta hai, aapko ise palat kar `R` nikalna hai.

key_points.title: Common Denominator
key_points.detail: Use LCM to create a common base before adding fractions.

key_points.title: Final Reciprocal
key_points.detail: Always flip the resulting fraction to find `R` instead of `1/R`.

steps.narration: Pehle `3` aur `6` ka LCM find karte hain.
Fractions ko common base par convert karte hain.
`R` nikalne ke liye fraction ko flip karte hain.
Denominators `10` aur `40` ka LCM lete hain.
Base same banakar fractions add karte hain.
Final answer ke liye flip karte hain.

common_mistakes.title: Forgetting the final flip
common_mistakes.explanation: `1/R = 1/2` nikalte hain aur `0.5` likh kar answer chhod dete hain. Isko flip karna zaruri hai taaki `R = 2` aa jaye.

common_mistakes.title: Adding numerators and denominators directly
common_mistakes.explanation: Fractions add karte time `1/3 + 1/6` ko `(1+1)/(3+6) = 2/9` likh dete hain jo mathematically bilkul galat hai.

recall_questions.q: What is the LCM of 2 and 4?
Why do we need inverse sums in physics?
recall_questions.answer: To calculate equivalent resistance in parallel and apply lens/mirror formulas.

recall_questions.q: What is the sum of 1/2 and 1/2?

oa_questions.question: Evaluate 1/R = 1/20 + 1/20
oa_questions.approach: Base is already common. 1/R = 2/20 = 1/10. Flip to get R = 10.
